questions.q: What is the ingestion layer's actual job in a system design?
options: Getting data from a source into storage reliably, before any cleaning or modeling happens
Aggregating data into business-ready reports
Enforcing the final star schema on incoming data
Serving cached query results to dashboards
questions.explain: Get this layer wrong, and everything downstream — partitioning, idempotency — is working with data that arrived incorrectly or incompletely.

questions.q: What actually decides whether an ingestion layer should be batch or streaming, per Lesson 5's framework?
options: Freshness requirements, not preference or sophistication
Whichever costs less regardless of the use case
Batch is always the correct default for ingestion
Streaming is always the correct default for ingestion
questions.explain: A nightly update calls for batch (like Autoloader watching a folder); 'as it happens' calls for streaming (an always-running Eventstream).

questions.q: When does an ingestion layer usually need schema-on-read instead of schema-on-write?
options: For a messy, less-controlled source, so the pipeline doesn't halt on a field it didn't anticipate
Schema-on-read should always be used, regardless of source quality
Only when the destination is a streaming system
Schema-on-read and schema-on-write are the same thing
questions.explain: A strict, well-governed source can afford schema-on-write and reject bad data immediately; a messy source usually can't.

questions.q: Why does the raw zone / bronze layer stay untouched, per DE Foundations Lesson 11 and Databricks Lesson 25?
options: So a cleansing bug discovered later can always be fixed by reprocessing from an untouched original
Because raw data is never actually stored anywhere
Because bronze tables cannot legally be modified after creation
Raw data is deleted automatically once it reaches the curated layer
questions.explain: Modifying raw data in place, even to 'fix' something, permanently loses the ability to redo that work correctly later.

questions.q: Where does deciding what 'clean' data means actually belong, according to this lesson?
options: In the transformation layer (Lesson 14), one layer after ingestion
In the ingestion layer itself, before any data is accepted
In the serving layer, after all transformations are complete
Cleaning decisions are made by the source system, never by the destination
questions.explain: Ingestion's job is landing data safely into the raw/bronze layer; cleaning is explicitly deferred to the next layer.
